paragraphs: A willingness to check dimensions, layout, material batches and drawings cell by cell, and to patiently correct misalignment or missing items, is a signal worth exploring further. Beyond liking the finished look, you also have to accept fine handwork, physical load and on-site collaboration.

First check the target job's kneeling, squatting and bending, lifting, dust, noise, tool training and pay conditions. One paper layout cannot prove you can build; cutting, tiling, demolition and work at height follow the corresponding training, on-site procedures and authorization.

Tile and stone setting, stone masonry, resilient flooring and carpet installation involve different materials and outputs; laying floors does not mean the skills are interchangeable. First choose a target by hard tile material, drawing and construction location.

Use the fictitious grid in the entry module E1 to calculate the number of units and the requirement for two colours, use E2 to handle a drawing version change, and write the material and handover record in E3. Use only paper and pen or a form; do not cut, mix adhesive or touch a job site or real customer data.
What should you experience first for tile and stone setting?

Start with dimension units, drawings and material checking: whether you can turn plane dimensions into a grid, distinguish colours and batches, and recompute and state the unknowns after a version change. You also need to understand the physical load, training and employment conditions; interest in a rendering alone is not enough.
This is an initial career exploration screen; the paper exercise does not replace skill training, construction assessment, project acceptance or a health evaluation.

More specific signals: a willingness to check the drawing row by row and column by column, to compare against material records, and to say which cell, version or batch the error occurred in. After a revision you keep the original record and separate what is known, assumed and to be confirmed, instead of claiming it is about right by eye.

Signals for caution include finding unit and version checking a nuisance, mixing different batches without recording, or ignoring on-site training and protection to rush the work. Extroversion, aesthetic sense or one fast calculation cannot replace task fit and a judgment of the working conditions.

Compare the drawings and shortfalls in E1 and E2 and check whether E3 lets someone else recompute. A willingness to find errors and keep improving supports learning more about the job; completing a paper work sample does not prove you can set tiles, cut or judge a substrate as acceptable independently.

US O*NET-SOC 47-2044.00 is Tile and Stone Setters: applying hard tile, stone and similar materials to walls, floors, ceilings, countertops and roofs. The Chinese name is a translated scope title and cannot be equated directly with a single Chinese trade or licence.

Inputs include drawings, setting-out patterns, surface dimensions, material specifications and site conditions. First check the units, version and scope, then estimate materials; when substrate, joint width or detail requirements are missing, ask the person in charge for clarification instead of filling them in as a construction design yourself.

Material quantities and positions are judged from blueprints, measurements and layout requirements. The editorial paper exercise extracts only the grid and version checking; real construction also involves substrate, bonding and detail conditions, so the exercise model cannot be copied over.

The output is hard tile surfaces, joints and related material records set and finished to requirements. O*NET also lists marble, granite and precast terrazzo tasks; a neat appearance cannot replace bonding, substrate or project acceptance.

Measure and mark the surface and check layout and positioning with a level, square, straightedge and similar tools. When you find a dimension conflict or a material shortfall, state the location, units, drawing version and actual records; do not build first and hide the difference afterwards.

Check drawings, materials and progress with the client, the site supervisor, other trades and suppliers. Cutting, fixing, demolition and substrate preparation all require the corresponding training and authorization; listing tasks does not grant structural design, hazardous work or acceptance authority.

The BLS precise occupation lists typical requirements of no formal educational credential, no related experience and long-term on-the-job training. This is a US group preparation measure, not a uniform Chinese entry condition, and does not mean no training is needed or that seven days is enough.

Check material specifications, drawings, quantities and to-be-confirmed items, and keep change and handover records. Hand unconfirmable substrate, detail or quality issues to the person in charge, and do not treat a shift handover record as acceptance.

The following two are editorially organized internal lines of work: tile setting centres on the pattern and joints of hard tiles, while stone installation also requires checking conditions by the specific stone specification and location. A job may cover only part of this and does not imply that experience transfers directly.

How are tile setting and stone installation distinguished?

Both work with hard tile, measurement and surface layout, but ceramic tile and natural stone differ in specification, material characteristics and installation location. The table below is an editorial summary; the specific substrate, fixing, bonding and acceptance bases must be confirmed by the project, and no on-site construction formula is provided.

Being able to install facing material does not mean holding structural design, work at height or lifting operation authority.
Key work judgments

Judgments rest on dimensions, drawings, materials and site evidence. The following are occupational understanding questions; the paper model ignores real construction conditions and cannot serve as a site material order or construction plan.
Do the dimensions, units and drawing version correspond to the same location?
Do the material colour, specification and batch match the drawing requirements?
Which parts of the estimate are assumptions and which need confirmation by the site supervisor?
After the drawing change, which quantities and positions need re-checking?

Keep the old and new versions and make clear which cells, materials and quantities changed. A correct paper calculation does not prove it can be set in practice; when joint width, cutting loss, substrate and details are unconfirmed, do not claim the site quantity is settled.
Does the task involve cutting dust, lifting or other hazardous work?

Check the training, protection, exposure control and on-site authority, and raise questions with the appropriate responsible person. This page does not instruct cutting, adhesive mixing, demolition, climbing or heavy stone lifting.
Which materials, details and quality statuses still need confirmation at handover?

Prepare | materials and quantity | compare the tile or stone specification, colour, batch and quantity, and distinguish the budget estimate from the approved quantity.

Section heading | the work environment of tile and stone setters

The work centres on hard tile, building surfaces and drawings. The US O*NET survey indicates that fine handwork, kneeling, squatting and bending, repetitive motions, noise and contaminants are worth knowing about; this is not the exposure intensity or health threshold of every Chinese site.

Organization and location | residential or commercial fit-out, new build and renovation projects divide work by trade. First check the specific material, location, project scale and employment relationship, and do not treat roofs, countertops and walls and floors as the same training scope.

Materials and tools | tile and stone, drawings, measuring tools, material and progress records. O*NET lists CAD, estimating, office and spreadsheet software background, which does not prove that all jobs require a particular software, AI tool or personally purchased cutting equipment.

Tasks are organized around drawings, materials, substrate and process sequencing. Dimensions, changes and detail items to be checked must be passed on accurately; the specific construction steps follow on-site approved conditions and training.

Time and intensity | check kneeling, squatting and bending, lifting, continuous work and rest arrangements. The merged BLS category notes that commercial sites may work evenings or weekends, which does not justify claiming that all tile jobs work shifts.
In communication, state the location, dimension units, drawing version, materials and missing items, and distinguish measurement results, estimating assumptions and unconfirmed conditions.

Chain of responsibility | execution, design, substrate confirmation, safety management and acceptance follow the actual division of labor. OSHA provides US silica dust background only; Chinese site-entry training, certificates and hazardous work requirements are checked by location and task.

Quality requirements | layout and materials match the drawing, changes are traceable and missing items are clear. A paper work sample only shows your calculation and recording approach and does not pass as real construction, quality acceptance or tool operation experience.

According to drawings and site conditions, set hard tile, stone and similar materials on walls, floors, countertops and similar locations, checking dimensions, layout, materials and joints, and completing installation and finishing. The US occupational scope also includes some roofing and decorative tasks; specific Chinese jobs and authority are checked separately.

Stonemasons produce stone walls, piers and other masonry, while this occupation focuses on setting hard facing material; sharing the word stone does not mean the structural responsibility or training is the same.

Resilient flooring installation works with sheet and tile flooring and the corresponding surfaces, and the occupational title explicitly excludes hard tile, carpet and wood flooring; experience cannot be swapped directly.

Brickmason and tile setter helpers carry out material, tool and clean-up support work and are a separate combined helper occupation; helper experience does not automatically prove you can set tiles independently.
Plastering and stucco work forms continuous plaster or decorative stucco and differs from installing hard tile; sharing a fit-out project does not mean the same output.

A task line within this occupation; substrate, material and tool training are checked by project.
Willing to check the drawing and dimensions cell by cell and to re-check in fine detail.
Stone laying and installation
Install and finish to the stone specification and location, checking materials, surfaces and related details.
Both fall within this occupation, but the specific materials and installation conditions are checked separately.
More interested in natural stone characteristics, dimensions and on-site interfaces.
Stonemasons
The focus shifts to stone structures and masonry, requiring additional masonry, structural and trade training.
If you care about stone walls or structures, you can check the target job; a setting work sample cannot pass as masonry ability.

The focus shifts to flexible sheet or tile flooring and the corresponding processes, requiring additional material and joint training.
If you care more about resilient flooring, you can re-check the target material and working conditions.

It carries support tasks with different responsibility and proficiency and cannot be seen as a renamed independent setter.
First learn the actual helper tasks, training and advancement conditions; no automatic upgrade is promised.
Plastering and stucco work
The output shifts to plaster and stucco finishes, requiring additional continuous surface and material training.
If you care more about smooth plastering, you can verify your ability as a new trade.
How do you choose between tile and stone work and adjacent trades?

First distinguish by output: hard facing material, stone structures, resilient flooring, support services or plaster surfaces. Even on the same fit-out site, the materials, responsibility and training differ.

After completing E1—E3, choose a job with a clear material and location and check the training, employment terms and work intensity; when turning to an adjacent direction, re-verify the corresponding skills.

The comparison is based on each precise O*NET occupational definition; the differences and selection signals are an editorial summary, not a transfer success rate, mutual qualification recognition or a demand ranking.

Can a text tool improve setting skills?

No corresponding causal study was obtained. Organizing lists can be an editorial trial use, but setting skills still require specific material, tool training and on-site feedback; generated word count cannot be treated as skill improvement.
Is the number of units a tool calculates the purchase quantity?

No. A paper grid ignores joint width, edge cutting, waste, substrate and details, and the actual quantity must be confirmed against the project basis. First re-check the units and model assumptions; do not order directly.
Does a drawing tool equal an AI adoption rate?
No. The O*NET software background describes software that may be used in the occupation and does not measure AI coverage, on-site reliability or time saved.

No. NIST is a voluntary risk method; Chinese on-site training, certificates, hazardous work and acceptance authority are still checked by local task and project.

600 millimetres = 0.6 metres; 3.0 ÷ 0.6 = 5 columns and 2.4 ÷ 0.6 = 4 rows, 20 cells in total; each cell is 0.36 square metres, total 7.2 square metres. In v1, every two rows give 5 of each colour, totalling 10 white and 10 grey: 2 white left over and 1 grey short.

entries.answer: Stonemasons build stone structures, resilient flooring and carpet work with different materials, and helpers carry out support work; sharing a site does not mean the training and responsibility are interchangeable.

entries.answer: You can do the E1—E3 fictitious grid, quantities, version change and handover with only paper and pen or a form, with no tools or site; it does not count as real construction experience.

entries.answer: The typical US measure is no formal educational credential and long-term on-the-job training; Chinese skill grades, local site entry and special tasks are checked by task separately, and the Beijing 2022 guideline is only a local example.

entries.answer: Insufficient evidence: no isolated net AI employment effect or score was obtained. A checklist can be trialled editorially, but the dimensions, drawings, site basis and responsibility need human checking.

entries.answer: US wages cannot be used to estimate personal compensation in China. In China, the 2025 pre-tax annual average for the broad production and manufacturing job group in above-scale enterprises is 80,739 yuan, covering construction and other personnel; the construction figures of 92,036 / 66,275 yuan for non-private / private belong to a different population. None is a separate median, starting wage or personal range for setters, and the gaps in the precise distribution and matching offers remain.

entries.answer: Check the actual material dust, kneeling and lifting, tool and on-site training, measurement, rework and payment; the OSHA material is US background and gives no Chinese permit or personal operating tutorial.
entries.question: Which risks should be checked first?

entries.answer: Observe the willingness to work with dimensions and drawings, record revisions, check details and collaborate, then check the training, physical load and actual conditions; RC is not a personality threshold.
entries.question: How do you judge fit?

entries.answer: The E1 grid and calculation, the E2 single-cell change and stock difference, and the E3 no-construction handover and unknowns list. Note the fictitious model and your own contribution, and do not call it project acceptance or a skill certificate.
